boundary_refinements.bukhari:2244:hi: The frozen first-pass note provisionally retained the final damaged sentence as context. Exact boundary review confirms that its opening dispatch-to-the-source-named-Kabzi clause is itself a complete finite historical action. That bounded clause is retained as a qualified fragment; only the broken ka-mamla/unassigned collective continuation remains context. No Urdu words, corrected name or missing answer is imported.
boundary_refinements.bukhari:2292:hi: Exact apparatus review separates the introductory Quran-verse label and its quotation/parenthesis delimiters from the actual cited verse words. Every verse word remains selected in Ibn Abbas’s source explanation; this refinement does not remove the heirs explanation, story bridge or brotherhood-domain qualification.
boundary_refinements.bukhari:2292:ur: Exact apparatus review separates the introductory Quran-verse label and its delimiters while preserving all actually cited Arabic words, including the source’s own formatting mark. The attributed explanation and its substantive qualifications are unchanged.

bukhari:2228.hi: Read the complete298-character Hindi field. Anas's own transmitted historical account names Safiyyah, Dihyah and the Prophet's marriage. Preserve the printed milin spelling and the supplied sequence without repairing or importing details. Honorific parentheses are part of the source; no explanatory apparatus is present.
bukhari:2228.ur: Read the complete255-character Urdu field independently. It supplies the same own narrated sequence from Anas: Safiyyah among captives, initially given to Dihyah, then marriage to the Prophet. Preserve the literal names/actions and do not infer an external identity link or add an unstated transaction.

bukhari:2230.hi: Read all237 Hindi characters. Jabir explicitly reports the Prophet selling a mudabbar slave, with the full printed chain. No missing definition, grade or legal explanation is supplied; retain the own finite action.
bukhari:2230.ur: Read all216 Urdu characters. The source itself attributes the finite sale action to the Prophet through Jabir. Keep mudabbar untranslated as the original source supplies it; no apparatus cut is needed.

bukhari:2231.hi: Read all209 Hindi characters. Amr heard Jabir report the Prophet's sale; this complete own action is eligible. Keep the source occurrence separate from2230 despite related wording.
bukhari:2231.ur: Read all181 Urdu characters. The own chain and finite sale statement explicitly name Jabir and the Messenger. Preserve all text and this independent source ID; no borrowed sentence or merged occurrence.

bukhari:2232.hi: Read all344 Hindi characters. Zayd and Abu Hurayrah relate an actual question and the Prophet's supplied answer. Preserve the unmarried condition, repeated actions and third-or-fourth uncertainty exactly; this is source classification, not present-day legal guidance or endorsement.
bukhari:2232.ur: Read all315 Urdu characters. The source independently supplies the named narrators, unmarried condition and actual dialogue. Preserve its third-or-fourth wording uncertainty and every condition without harmonization.

bukhari:2233.hi: Read all344 characters of this separately saved Hindi field. Its repeated question/answer and third-or-fourth alternative remain literal. Do not collapse2233 into2232 even where their full strings match.
bukhari:2233.ur: Read all315 characters of this independently supplied Urdu field. It contains the same actual source dialogue with its own saved identity; retain the unmarried and recurrence conditions and unresolved count, without deduplicating the parent.

bukhari:2239.hi: Read all575 Hindi characters. Ibn Abbas's Medina trade-practice account contains Ismail's explicit uncertainty over one/two versus two/three years, followed by the Prophet's measure-or-weight instruction. Keep the Medina population qualifier and the parenthetic duration predicate; both define actual source scope. The reported duration uncertainty must stay visibly attached to the account and must not be assigned as Prophetic uncertainty.
bukhari:2239.ur: Read all526 Urdu characters independently. Preserve the same own printed alternative durations, their explicit Ismail attribution, the parenthetic people-of-Medina domain and duration predicate. The Prophet's actual instruction here says measure OR weight; do not replace it with the conjunction printed in another occurrence.

bukhari:2239.2.ar: Read all133 Arabic characters. The chain ends bihadha and only a prepositional measure/weight fragment. No complete predicate or command is supplied; this supports source-only disposition without importing another occurrence.
bukhari:2239.2.en: Read all66 English characters. The abbreviated as-above wording mentions only specific measure and stops there. Do not add weight or a command absent from this own field.
bukhari:2239.2.hi: Read all92 characters. This is a same-way transmission pointer plus the nouns known measure/known weight. It supplies no finite report body or directive; retain full source context.
bukhari:2239.2.ur: Read all84 characters. The own field only mentions a same-way report and quoted measure/weight nouns. No body is filled from2239; full context is required.
bukhari:2239.2.ur-Latn: Read all103 Roman Urdu characters. Same-way transmission and quoted measure/weight nouns only; no actual finite matn. Every nonempty sibling has now been read and supports resolved source-only context.

bukhari:2240.hi: Read all485 Hindi characters. Ibn Abbas reports the Medina date practice and an explicit Prophetic instruction for specified weight and term. Keep the two/three years and the actual weight/term wording; do not import a missing measure term from another source ID.
bukhari:2240.ur: Read all429 Urdu characters independently. The chain, historical practice and Prophet's stated weight/term instruction are complete as supplied. Preserve the literal own version without harmonizing it to2239 or2240.2.

bukhari:2240.2.hi: Read all145 Hindi characters. Ibn Abi Najih reports an actual finite advance-payment instruction attributed only to the respectful aap with a printed honorific. Do not invent a more explicit name from neighboring2240; admit as a qualified abbreviated instruction with the source's pronominal/honorific speaker identity. The salaf parenthesis is a lexical synonym, retained as context.
bukhari:2240.2.ur: Read all132 Urdu characters. The own text establishes a finite command and an explicitly respectful pronoun, but does not spell out the person's name. Preserve that qualified source attribution without borrowing identity. The parenthetic salaf label defines advance payment and is lexical context.

bukhari:2241.hi: Read all382 Hindi characters. Ibn Abbas explicitly names the Prophet's arrival and instruction. The source-parenthetic Medina is an actual supplied destination; the bai-salam parenthesis supplies the instruction's transaction domain. Retain those meaningful arguments and honorifics, rather than broadening the instruction into a context-free rule.
bukhari:2241.ur: Read all342 Urdu characters independently. The Prophet is explicitly named, with source-parenthetic arrival location and advance-sale subject. Preserve the reported destination and the essential transaction-domain predicate without external confirmation or added detail.

bukhari:2242.hi: Read all450 Hindi characters. Preserve the reporter's explicit Muhammad-or-Abdullah identity alternative. The inquiry and Ibn Abi Awfa's historical collective trade practice across the Prophet/Abu Bakr/Umar periods are finite source content. The final own inquiry/confirmatory response from Ibn Abza is a narrated event referring to a body already supplied in this field, not a reconstructed new quotation. The two advance-trade terminology parentheses are lexical context.
bukhari:2242.ur: Read all410 Urdu characters. The own name alternative, disagreement, visit and quoted historical practice remain, followed by the narrator's actual second inquiry/confirmation. Do not choose between the source's two narrator names or claim an expanded Ibn Abza quotation. The synonymous salaf/advance-transaction labels are context.

bukhari:2243.hi: Read this complete450-character Hindi field separately. It supplies the own name uncertainty, inquiry, Ibn Abi Awfa historical answer and narrated Ibn Abza confirmation. Preserve the source's local spelling differences and separate occurrence identity. Only the two lexical transaction labels are apparatus.
bukhari:2243.ur: Read this complete410-character Urdu field independently. Retain its actual inquiry/testimony and name alternative under this source ID, including the within-field confirmatory reply without synthesizing repeated words. The two lexical synonyms remain context.

bukhari:2244.hi: Read all591 Hindi characters. The initial inquiry and Abdullah's wheat-only testimony and answer are coherent actual source content. Preserve the defective source names/spellings. The final sentence splices a sending-to-Abd-al-Rahman-bin-Kabzi phrase into an unmarked ka-mamla/first-person continuation, with missing wording and uncertain voice; retain this damaged continuation as context without repairing it from Urdu. The salaf synonym is lexical context.
bukhari:2244.ur: Read all668 Urdu characters independently. This field supplies a complete Ibn Abi Awfa inquiry/testimony with wheat, barley and olives, followed by a separately named Abd al-Rahman ibn Abza question/answer. Keep both actual speakers and their own reported practices distinct. Do not delete the extra goods to match Hindi or repair Hindi from this field; the salaf synonym alone is lexical context.

bukhari:2245.hi: Read all201 Hindi characters. The own abbreviated source supplies a finite collective trade-practice statement through Muhammad ibn Abi al-Mujalid, then Shaybani's olive addition and another finite wheat/barley/raisin wording. Preserve these actual qualified transmitted fragments without inventing an unseen Ibn Abi Awfa speaker or a Prophetic era; the olive noun addition is explicitly tied to the finite predicate already present in this same field.
bukhari:2245.ur: Read all197 Urdu characters independently. The first reported we voice and the two expressly Shaybani-introduced variants are actual own-field content. Keep their distinct transmitted roles and the within-field additive object; do not treat Shaybani as a new eyewitness to an unprinted time or import the preceding record's authority.

bukhari:2246.hi: Read all797 characters. Abu al-Bakhtari's actual inquiry elicits Ibn Abbas's explicitly attributed Prophetic prohibition. A different unnamed questioner and a man sitting near Ibn Abbas then exchange an actual meaning question/answer; the latter man's estimate explanation is a reported anonymous utterance, not the compiler's gloss and not Ibn Abbas's or the Prophet's words. Separate those voices. The final Mu'adh/Shu'bah route ends in an objectless forbade plus same-hadith pointer and supplies no further body; retain that entire transmission tail as context.
bukhari:2246.ur: Read all740 Urdu characters independently. Keep the actual Ibn Abbas/Prophetic prohibition and the distinct unnamed conversation about what weighing means. The printed answer here says capable of estimation; do not replace it with the harvest/storage answer in2249. The Mu'adh chain and same-hadith ending are context without reconstructing the omitted object.

bukhari:2247.hi: Read all594 characters. Abu al-Bakhtari recounts two actual inquiries: Ibn Umar's report contains the date-readiness and deferred silver/gold prohibitions; Ibn Abbas's report contains its own eaten-or-edible and weight wording. Keep the two attributed report components separate. The advance-transaction definition parenthesis is lexical context; honorifics and all conditions remain.
bukhari:2247.ur: Read all571 characters independently. The own field names both Companion respondents and supplies their actual Prophetic reports. Preserve the different predicates and the or alternative in the second report. Retain the lexical advance-transaction gloss as context and do not infer a merged narration.

bukhari:2248.hi: Read this separate complete594-character Hindi field. The Ibn Umar and Ibn Abbas replies remain two actual attributed components under this source ID, with all conditions literal. The parenthetic trade definition is context; matching wording does not authorize merging2248 with2247.
bukhari:2248.ur: Read this separate complete571-character Urdu field. Preserve both own named responses, the supplied currencies, conditions and alternative readiness phrasing. The glossary parenthesis is context, and no source ID or language text is deduplicated.

bukhari:2249.hi: Read all650 characters. The source supplies Ibn Umar's report, Ibn Abbas's report, then the narrator's weighing question answered by an unnamed person sitting beside Ibn Abbas. Keep that final actual quoted explanation under its anonymous speaker, not the Prophet or Ibn Abbas. Its own answer says cut and stored; do not harmonize it to2246's estimation wording.
bukhari:2249.ur: Read all624 characters independently. Three actual voice groups are supplied: Ibn Umar relaying the Prophet, Ibn Abbas relaying the Prophet, and the unnamed seated man's reply. Preserve all source conditions and the specific cut/storage interpretation as that man's quoted answer. No compiler gloss or external legal conclusion is added.

bukhari:2250.hi: Read this complete650-character Hindi field separately. Retain both named Companion reports and the anonymous seated man's actual answer as distinct components. Preserve this occurrence despite repeated wording, and do not reassign the final interpretation to the Prophet.
bukhari:2250.ur: Read this complete624-character Urdu field independently. Keep its three supplied voice groups and the exact harvest/storage answer without textual harmonization or duplicate-parent removal. All text is actual report/dialogue apart from no independently identified apparatus here.

bukhari:2251.hi: Read all345 Hindi characters. Aisha explicitly reports the Prophet's credit purchase of grain from an unnamed Jewish man and his iron-armour pledge. Preserve the source's exact parties, actions and chain; no counterparty name, external identity or commentary is added.
bukhari:2251.ur: Read all310 Urdu characters independently. The own field supplies Aisha's actual credit-purchase/pledge report. Retain the literal iron armour and unnamed counterparty; all text is reported content with its chain.

bukhari:2253.hi: Read all589 characters. Ibn Abbas's actual Medina trade practice and Prophetic measure/term instruction are complete. The Abdullah ibn Walid/Sufyan/Ibn Abi Najih transmission tail also supplies a finite alternate instruction because its own parenthesis explicitly states that bai-salam should occur. Retain the quoted measure/weight plus that affirmative predicate as a qualified transmitted variant of the same report, with its bare chain/comparison introduction as context. This differs from2239.2's noun-only fragment.
bukhari:2253.ur: Read all538 Urdu characters. Preserve the actual two/three-year practice and Prophet's stated measure/term direction. The final own quoted measure/weight phrase and parenthetic bai-salam-should-be predicate together supply a finite transmitted variant; keep both, under the explicitly introduced route, without filling other text or identifying a new eyewitness.

bukhari:2254.hi: Read all508 Hindi characters. Muhammad's inquiry names Abd al-Rahman ibn Abza and Abdullah ibn Abi Awfa, who answer jointly about their own historical practice, spoils, Syrian Nabataeans and the farm question. Retain their collective attribution, commodities and specified term. The parenthetic salam synonym is lexical context; do not divide the unassigned joint answer between invented individual speakers.
bukhari:2254.ur: Read all486 Urdu characters independently. The own field supplies the two named respondents' joint first-person account and the narrator's follow-up question. Preserve the named collective voice and the statement that they did not ask about cultivation. Only the synonymous transaction-term parenthesis is context.

bukhari:2255.hi: Read this complete508-character Hindi field separately. It has its own supplied collective report and follow-up inquiry, with both named respondents. Preserve every source word and this separate occurrence; the salam synonym remains context.
bukhari:2255.ur: Read this complete486-character Urdu field independently. The same own joint-response structure, historical details and no-inquiry statement stay literal. The source ID is not merged with2254, and the lexical transaction label is kept as context.

bukhari:2256.hi: Read all342 characters. The source names the reporter only Abdullah; do not expand that name from an assumed chain. It gives the historical trading practice and the Prophet's prohibition. The final explanation is explicitly attributed to Nafi, not the Prophet; preserve it as Nafi's own quoted source clarification in a separately typed component of the same transaction report. Its printed jaan-le wording is defective/different from the Urdu birth verb and must remain unrepaired.
bukhari:2256.ur: Read all318 characters independently. Abdullah's report of practice/prohibition is followed by Nafi's expressly attributed quoted explanation of habal al-habalah. Keep the actual source Nafi voice distinct from the Prophet, preserving its own birth wording and the main report's abbreviated Abdullah name. Do not repair or harmonize the Hindi field.

bukhari:2257.hi: Read all422 Hindi characters. Jabir reports the Prophet's preemption award and the source-stated limit once boundaries/roads are established. Keep the limit attached so the award is not broadened; describe it as a reported qualification, not an invented extra direct Prophetic quotation.
bukhari:2257.ur: Read all383 Urdu characters independently. The own field supplies both the award and the subsequent boundary/road condition. Preserve the complete scope and Jabir's transmitted attribution without assigning unprinted direct-speech quotation marks or dropping the consequence.

bukhari:2259.hi: Read all463 characters. The two printed chains lead to Aisha's actual gift-priority question and the Prophet's nearer-door answer. Keep both chains and the own dialogue; the second-chain label itself is apparatus, retained separately.
bukhari:2259.ur: Read all432 Urdu characters. The own source explicitly attributes the question to Aisha and the answer to the Prophet. Preserve the two-neighbor and nearer-door conditions. Only the parenthetical second-isnad label is apparatus; no narration wording is rewritten.

bukhari:2261.hi: Read all631 characters. Abu Musa reports his visit with two Ash'ar men, his lack of prior knowledge of their wish and the Prophet's appointment response. The my-tribe parenthesis is an identifying gloss. The final unnamed narrator comparison of lan/la is visible transmission apparatus, as in the equivalent-formula17 calibration, not a new narration component; preserve it fully in context and mention the unresolved wording. Do not alter the actual main negation.
bukhari:2261.ur: Read all581 Urdu characters independently. Preserve the actual visit, Abu Musa's statement and the source's complete refusal wording. The parenthetic tribe identification is context, and the final unnamed lan/la uncertainty remains verbatim transmission context, not silently resolved or attributed as another Prophetic statement.

bukhari:2263.hi: Read all866 Hindi characters. The own field contains a historical hiring/journey report explicitly naming the Prophet and Abu Bakr. Preserve its shortened chain, defective name/spellings such as the feminine Aisa form and ghar-i-taur, and every supplied action without repairing them from Urdu. The migration-time parenthesis is actual narrative scope. The entire kharrit dictionary explanation is compiler/translator context; the skilled-guide hiring and actual alliance/trust/travel account remain.
bukhari:2263.ur: Read all892 Urdu characters independently. Aisha's own full chain and the hiring, alliance, trust, three-night appointment and coastal journey are supplied. Retain the migration temporal scope. Separate only the kharrit lexical-definition clause; no external guide name or canonical route is inserted, and the extra chain names are not transferred into Hindi.

bukhari:2265.hi: Read all816 Hindi characters. Ya'la's own best-deeds assessment belongs to his actual narrative, followed by the servant fight and Prophetic judgment/dialogue. Retain the complaint-purpose parenthesis as actual narrative framing; the parenthetic Tabuk battle-name identification is apparatus. The final Ibn Jurayj/Abdullah ibn Abi Mulaykah/grandfather route supplies a finite similar biting case with Abu Bakr's judgment: keep that bounded report separately attributed and do not harmonize the two judges or invent the unnamed grandfather's identity.
bukhari:2265.ur: Read all760 Urdu characters independently. Preserve Ya'la's personal testimony, the unresolved biter identities and the Prophet's full actual answer. The Tabuk label is context, while the complaint action is narrative. The later finite Abu Bakr judgment belongs to its own expressly transmitted similar report, not to the Prophet's speech or an automatic identity merge.

bukhari:2266.hi: Read this separate complete816-character Hindi field. Ya'la's testimony and the Prophetic biting-case judgment are followed by a fully supplied similar Abu Bakr judgment through Ibn Jurayj's route. Preserve the two actual report authorities and separate source ID; only the Tabuk identification label is apparatus, while the complaint purpose and Ya'la's own assessment remain narrative.
bukhari:2266.ur: Read this separate complete760-character Urdu field independently. Keep the supplied Ya'la/Prophet episode and the later grandfather-transmitted Abu Bakr case as distinct typed components. Do not infer the biter's name, the grandfather's expanded identity or a shared event merely from similar wording. The battle label is context; complaint scope stays.

bukhari:2274.hi: Read all494 characters. Ibn Abbas explicitly relays the Prophet's prohibition and then answers the source questioner's meaning question. Keep the trade-caravan and going-out-beyond-the-market qualifiers because removing them broadens the prohibition into ordinary encounters. The later broker explanation is Ibn Abbas's actual quoted answer, not compiler dictionary apparatus; separate its speaker from the Prophet.
bukhari:2274.ur: Read all455 Urdu characters. Preserve the actual trade/market scope parentheses and the explicit Ibn Abbas interpretive answer. The source's questioner remains its supplied first-person voice without an expanded name; the answer is not reassigned as Prophetic speech.

bukhari:2275.hi: Read all960 characters. Khabbab's actual labour/debt dialogue with As ibn Wa'il includes their respective oaths and the reported revelation quotation. Keep the supplied Quran transliteration and translation because they form the source's actual quoted consequence, not an appended citation label. The parenthetic polytheist category is biographical apparatus. Do not attribute As's hostile statements or the Quran quotation as new Prophetic speech.
bukhari:2275.ur: Read all906 characters independently. Preserve Khabbab's own historical dialogue, the counterparty's words and the actually supplied Arabic verse with its Urdu rendering. The revelation context remains explicit; the parenthetic identity category alone is context. No absent verse number, translation correction or external testimony is added.

bukhari:2276.hi: Read all2085 Hindi characters, including the complete end. Abu Sa'id reports the Companions' journey, denied hospitality, snakebite, payment agreement, actual recited opening, recovery, subsequent inquiry and the Prophet's reply/laughter. Keep the source's anonymous healer and other participants unnamed, the full narrative conditions, actual alhamdu recitation and Fatiha name in the dialogue. The final Shu'bah/Abu Bishr/Abu Mutawakkil same-hearing tail supplies no further body and stays transmission context. No medical advice or extra healing formula is generated.
bukhari:2276.ur: Read all1931 Urdu characters independently, through the final chain note. The own field supplies the full episode and actual Arabic recitation phrase; keep them with the distinct narrator, anonymous Companions and Prophet. The Surah Fatiha name here is substantive dialogue, not a verse locator. The final same-hearing chain note remains context; do not fill a complete surah, identify the healer or infer an external matched report.

bukhari:2277.hi: Read all397 characters. Anas reports Abu Taybah's cupping, the Prophet's payment instruction and intercession about the imposed levy. Preserve the source's one-or-two measure uncertainty and all named/unnamed roles; do not settle the amount or rewrite the source's transliteration.
bukhari:2277.ur: Read all358 Urdu characters independently. The own field supplies the cupping/payment/intercession report with explicit one-or-two-sa alternative. Keep that uncertainty, the owners and the reduction request without adding a missing amount or a modern recommendation.

bukhari:2278.hi: Read all362 characters. Ibn Abbas's named reporting frame supplies the Prophet's cupping/payment action followed by a conditional inference that he would not have done/paid if it were impermissible. Keep the actual practice separate from the source reporting voice's inferential saying, never as additional Prophetic speech. No claim of independent jurisprudential endorsement is made.
bukhari:2278.ur: Read all334 Urdu characters. The own source reports the Prophetic action and then the reporter's finite conditional reasoning. Its attribution remains the source's Ibn Abbas reporting frame, with a distinct non-Prophetic inference type; no new speaker or directly spoken Prophetic legal sentence is invented.

bukhari:2279.hi: Read all319 characters. The own Ibn Abbas report supplies cupping/payment and then a finite rhetorical condition about dislike/payment. Preserve that latter saying as the reporting voice's inference, separately from the Prophet's narrated actions and without correcting its colloquial phrasing.
bukhari:2279.ur: Read all289 Urdu characters independently. Keep the actual cupping and payment report, then the source reporter's rhetorical inference with its printed awkward phrasing. It is not assigned to the Prophet as spoken dialogue; no external legal conclusion is added.

bukhari:2283.hi: Read all259 characters. Abu Hurayrah explicitly reports the Prophet's prohibition concerning the printed source category of earnings. The complete own chain/body is retained as a historical attributed report, without new legal advice or altered terminology.
bukhari:2283.ur: Read all224 Urdu characters. The own field supplies the named narrator and finite Prophetic prohibition. Preserve it exactly with the chain; there is no distinct lexical or locator apparatus here.

bukhari:2284.hi: Read all271 characters. Ibn Umar explicitly reports a prohibition on the named fee category. Preserve the source-defective/opaque nar-kadanay term exactly, without replacing it with an inferred standard wording or importing an Arabic definition from an unread sibling.
bukhari:2284.ur: Read all241 Urdu characters independently. Ibn Umar's own finite attributed prohibition is clear as a report, while the compact source term narkadanay remains literal. No corrected term, external canonical linkage or independently certified interpretation is added.

bukhari:2289.hi: Read all1558 Hindi characters. Salamah ibn al-Akwa recounts three successive funerals with their distinct debt/estate answers and the Prophet's actions, ending with Abu Qatadah's actual guarantee. Preserve each case and the printed three-dinar amounts without mixing debt and estate, naming an anonymous deceased, or converting three narrative cases into new source IDs.
bukhari:2289.ur: Read all1406 Urdu characters independently. The own source supplies the complete three-case dialogue and Abu Qatadah's undertaking. Keep the respective questions, absence/presence of assets/debt and the eventual prayer intact. This remains a narrated report, not current legal or financial guidance.

bukhari:2292.hi: Read all922 Hindi characters. Ibn Abbas is explicitly the source speaker explaining the supplied Quran terms and the historical Muhajir/Ansar inheritance arrangement established by the Prophet. Keep the actual quoted/transliterated Quran, the heirs explanation, narrative bridge and the brotherhood-domain qualifier of the revoked inheritance rule; these belong to the attributed explanation and its scope, not appended verse locators. The final parenthetical comparison to other persons and one-third-estate execution reads as appended legal explanation and is retained as complete source context with its limitation explicitly noted, rather than newly attributed as Prophetic speech or silently discarded.
bukhari:2292.ur: Read all844 Urdu characters independently. The own Ibn Abbas explanation contains actual Arabic quotations, the heirs meaning and a finite historical account plus the source-stated limitation of the revoked arrangement. Preserve those terms, qualifications and supplied sequence. The final separate parenthetical one-third/legal-execution explanation remains verbatim source context; acknowledge its presence so the shortened quotation is not represented as the complete surrounding legal discussion. No present-day legal conclusion or external verse identity is added.

bukhari:2293.hi: Read all288 characters. Anas reports the Prophet establishing brotherhood between the source-named Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf and Sa'd ibn Rabi. Preserve the full actual chain and action, without merging it into2292's different source account.
bukhari:2293.ur: Read all257 Urdu characters independently. The source explicitly names the participants and Prophetic action. Keep the separate occurrence and complete supplied wording; no commentary apparatus needs removal.

bukhari:2299.hi: Read all363 Hindi characters. Ali explicitly reports a Prophetic command to give the sacrificed animals' coverings and hides as charity. Preserve those supplied objects and the source's own spelling; no meat or other absent instruction is added.
bukhari:2299.ur: Read all331 Urdu characters. The own chain and Ali's stated command are finite source content. Preserve the sacrificed-animal qualification, coverings and hides exactly; no inferred companion detail or alternate edition is imported.

bukhari:2301.hi: Read all1622 Hindi characters. Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf recounts his agreement with Umayyah, the explicit family-or-property uncertainty, name discussion and Badr protection/pursuit episode with Bilal's actual words. The parenthetic unbeliever/enemy category is explanatory identity apparatus, while the arriving-group parenthesis supplies the actor of the attempted distraction and remains meaningful narrative scope. Keep the source violence and names as historical report without praise, correction or advocacy. The final third-person statement that Abd al-Rahman showed us his scar belongs to an unnamed witness voice and must be a separately attributed finite observation, not made part of Abd al-Rahman's first-person speech or assigned a guessed narrator.
bukhari:2301.ur: Read all1534 Urdu characters independently, including its source typographic defect near the group reaching them. Preserve the treaty, the alternative family/property object, all reported dialogue/actions and the actual arriving-group subject. Separate the parenthetic ideological category as context. The final we-saw-scar testimony is actual source content under an unspecified later witness voice, distinct from Abd al-Rahman's autobiographical report; neither voice is converted to Prophetic speech.
